thesis: Record inflows and ~10pt margin expansion look exceptional, but Q1 flows were concentrated in one $16B St. James's Place enhanced mandate and management flagged a fee-rate headwind next quarter from mix shift, which the market may take weeks to discount.
red_flags: Q1 net flows heavily reliant on a single $16B enhanced mandate; CFO conceded fee-rate 'headwind in the next quarter' from continued mix shift to lower-fee enhanced; managed-vol still a slight outflow.

thesis: Commercial base is flat (~$73.6M FY) and the equity story rests on a binary Q2 LOTIS-5 readout while management anchors investors to an aspirational $600M-$1B peak that hinges on approvals and compendia inclusion the market cannot yet underwrite.
red_flags: Every peak-revenue figure tagged 'assuming compendia inclusion and regulatory approval'; strong Q4 revenue attributed to 'variability in customer ordering patterns' rather than durable demand; underlying volume flat; ongoing net losses funded by PIPEs.

thesis: Record backlog ($2.9B) and disciplined selection into a booming gas/data-center power build-out, but FY27 margins are explicitly unguided and will normalize off a Trumbull-boosted 20.5%, a mean-reversion nuance the market digests slowly.
red_flags: CFO declined FY27 gross-margin guidance ('too early to tell'); FY26 margin flattered by Trumbull excess margin (quarterly margins have ranged 11.4%-25%); reliance on lumpy large-project timing ('handful of new projects over 12-20 months').

thesis: Record EPS (+19%) and 54% ROE with heavy capital return, but management is candidly flagging multi-quarter flow headwinds (Comerica adviser departures through Q3, cautious clients, disciplined recruiting pullback) that mute the growth optics, a tension the market prices in slowly.
red_flags: 'Lighter on flows' and 'lumpiness in recruiting and terminations'; Comerica outflows to persist Q2-Q3; asset management still in net outflows (-$5.9B); ~$48B parked in third-party money funds not yet redeployed; RPS earnings only reaffirmed at ~$800M/yr.

thesis: Fully utilized fleet and a building order book against 160-week equipment lead times, yet management held FY guidance despite a Q1 beat out of early-year conservatism, so the embedded beat-and-raise potential may only be recognized over subsequent quarters.
red_flags: Guidance reaffirmed (not raised) despite Q1 exceeding the basis for guidance; SG&A elevated by a $3.7M one-time comp acceleration (said non-recurring); internal inconsistency in stated FY EBITDA top end ($950M vs $915M); CFO retirement transition underway.

thesis: Volume inflected positive (first sales increase since 2022) on data-center/solar demand and management held EBITDA/EPS guidance, but cable-segment margin compression from copper/aluminum and an unresolved strategic review leave the profit trajectory ambiguous, a mixed signal the market resolves over weeks.
red_flags: Adjusted EPS down sharply YoY ($1.23 vs $2.04); cable (~17% of sales) seeing 'significant spread compression'; net-sales guide lowered (divestiture-driven); $136.5M PVC antitrust settlement covers only 2 of 3 classes; strategic-review outcome open-ended.

thesis: Management declares the turnaround complete and issues accelerating FY27 guidance (top end ~15% growth vs 3% in FY26) backed by a growing ~$950M QNX royalty backlog and a secure-comms inflection to first growth in 6 years, a re-rating from 'restructuring' to 'growth' story the market may take weeks to underwrite.
red_flags: FY27 guide hedged, management 'price[d] in some risk to the lower end' on macro uncertainty; QNX Q1 guided sequentially lower ($60-64M vs $78.7M) with repeated 'don't judge quarter-to-quarter' framing; Alloy core has 'no design wins yet'; licensing revenue came in slightly below guidance.

thesis: Sustained women's/kids denim momentum (women's +12%, fifth straight double-digit quarter; kids +16%) plus a doubling of planned new-store openings (6 to 12-14) signals management confidence in a physical-expansion re-acceleration, even without formal guidance, and is slow to digest given men's softness.
red_flags: No guidance per company policy; men's business soft (sales -0.5%, denim -3.5%) and footwear -3%; inventory up 15.5% YoY (ahead of ~5% sales growth, markdown risk); growth leaning on price (AUR +5.5%) with UPTs down ~1.5%; cash flow not disclosed in release.

thesis: A 1M-ton Centurion volume cut (3.5M to 2.5M) and higher met-coal costs are set against a sharp Middle East/Indonesia-driven seaborne thermal upcycle, so the market must weigh a fixable operational stumble against improving thermal fundamentals over the coming weeks.
red_flags: Centurion FY sales cut to 2.5M from 3.5M tons and met cost guide raised to $123-133/ton; met segment posted an EBITDA loss (-$7M) with Centurion ramp cutting ~$80M; multiple fuel-driven cost-guidance increases; Centurion recovery is projected ('largely confined to Q2'), not yet realized; rare-earth/germanium details withheld 'for proprietary reasons.'
